prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1240; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim received by phone from the insured driver reporting a low-speed head-on collision at a residential intersection. Insured states the other vehicle crossed the center line on a curve. Police report requested. Vehicle is drivable but front bumper and hood damaged. Photos requested from insured.

Entry 2: Claimant's representing attorney's office contacted this adjuster and confirmed representation. Letter of representation on file. All further communication to be routed through counsel. Claimant reports a wrist fracture sustained in the impact and is currently under orthopedic care. Medical authorization requested through counsel.

Entry 3: Inspection of both vehicles completed at the repair facility. Damage consistent with a low-speed frontal impact. Airbag deployment noted on the claimant's vehicle. Estimator to finalize repair scope. Supplemental photos saved to file.

Entry 4: Received preliminary medical records from claimant's treating provider through counsel. Records document a closed distal radius fracture, casted, with follow-up scheduled. Reviewing records for relationship to the reported collision. Requested prior medical history for the same wrist to rule out pre-existing condition.

Entry 5: Spoke with claimant's counsel regarding the status of the file. Counsel indicated a demand package will follow once treatment is complete. Liability appears probable against the other driver based on the police report and statements. Reserves reviewed and adjusted for bodily injury and property damage. File remains open pending medical updates.
